A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from RelationBooth to DreamRelation. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, and qualitative generations, including additional experiments in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds comparator scores, three-object examples, and a keypoint-alignment diagnostic.

M1.justification: The renamed method retains the synthetic triplet data engine, MS-Diffusion/SDXL foundation, text-attention LoRA, keypoint matching loss, and self-distilled local tokens. Expanded descriptions of inherited attention and coordinate handling do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds customization involving three objects in Figure 8, extending the earlier single-object and object-pair evaluations. The datasets and relation vocabulary remain unchanged; SDXL relation inversion and CogVideoX demonstrations already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: v3 adds Mix-of-Show to the Figure 1 comparison and ReVersion+MS to the quantitative RelationBench comparison and Figure 6. The analogous relation-inversion+MS comparison already appeared in v1 Figure 4, so this extends its evaluated participation rather than introducing an entirely new comparator.

E3.justification: The data-engine ablation changes from blank image prompts in v1 Section 4.2 to objects cropped from target images in v3. Many published RelationBench prompts are shortened or given different contexts (v1 Table 9; v3 Table 10). Training budgets and evaluation counts remain unchanged; these revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a KML latent-similarity diagnostic and three-object generalization examples, revises the data-engine control, and removes the single-object component-ablation results. Encoder, token-count, injection-method, and loss-weight ablations remain, including those relocated to supplementary material.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The same-random-seed statement for qualitative ablations is retained.

E6.justification: DreamBench CLIP-I/DINO change from 78.9/67.4 to 81.7/68.4, and M-CustomConcept101 CLIP-T changes from 29.4 to 29.7. v3 also adds ReVersion+MS scores and qualitative findings, revises several multi-object ablation values, and removes single-object ablation entries. Existing RelationBench comparison scores remain identical; the revised data-engine ablation uses different conditions.

T1.justification: v3 revises the mathematical attention specification by including the bounding-box mask M in Equation 4 and explaining it through Equation 2; v1's Equation 4 omits this term. This is a limited mathematical clarification, with no new theorem, proof, or theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain relation-aware customization, an identity-disentangling data engine, keypoint matching, and local-token injection. The claimed combination of relation fidelity and identity preservation is retained despite renaming and rewritten presentation.

C2.justification: v3 expands explanations involving overlapping bounding boxes and the need for detailed object-part features. Section 11 newly states that CogVideoX handles simple interactions such as shaking hands but struggles with hugging. The original image-generation failure cases and societal-impact discussion remain.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly documents keypoint-coordinate rescaling, ReVersion integrations, Mix-of-Show implementation, and using generated images as CogVideoX first frames. It removes the 13 MB LoRA-storage statement. Core hyperparameters, hardware, training time, and distillation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including ADI, MultiBooth, DINO, Transformers, and Adam, while dropping the Mask R-CNN reference. Its new capability-comparison Table 1 makes research positioning more explicit, but the central relationship to customization and relation-inversion research remains.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming, v3 extensively rewrites the introduction, related work, motivation, and method explanations. It reorganizes supplementary sections, separates failure cases, and moves references before the supplementary material, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column layout, adds a capability table and new diagnostic/example figures, redraws the architecture and data-engine diagrams, and annotates comparison failures. Numerous existing figures and tables are relocated or rearranged, including stacked ablation and feature-visualization panels.

improvement.justification: Explicit comparator evaluations, three-object examples, and the KML alignment diagnostic modestly strengthen the empirical support, while clearer explanations improve readability. These gains are limited by the removal of single-object ablations and insufficient explanation connecting revised prompts and numerical results to the reported experiments.
